source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Obtain or restore access to the indicated PPE before entering for anticipated exposure, and report supply problems through the facility process.","B":"Enter without the indicated PPE and obtain it later if visible contamination occurs, because precautions begin only after an exposure is seen.","C":"Ask staff to bring personal protective supplies from home because institutional PPE availability is not part of infection-control readiness.","D":"Ignore the shortage until the next shift because Transmission-Based Precautions do not require the appropriate PPE to be available before patient contact."}}
source_row.rationale: The indicated PPE must be available and donned before anticipated exposure under Transmission-Based Precautions. A supply shortage should be corrected/escalated rather than bypassing required protection.
source_row.source_detail: Transmission-Based Precautions guidance requires use of the indicated PPE in addition to Standard Precautions based on route of transmission; PPE should be donned before relevant patient/environment contact or exposure. Current CDC Transmission-Based Precautions page rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A nurse finds that the PPE needed for a client's Transmission-Based Precautions is not readily available before care. What is the best action?
